obligations.note: No changes to rbac.py or access-policy.json; the new route reuses the existing manage_payees action already in the approved matrix. The access matrix is unchanged and remains default-deny.
The auditor role's permissions are untouched; the new route requires manage_payees which the auditor does not hold. No state-changing action is added to the auditor.
The new route uses manage_payees, not approve_payment or release_payment. The it_admin role's segregation of duties is unaffected.

The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen uses action manage_payees, which is in the privileged list in access-policy.json, yet is declared with mfa=False. The CI test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails explicitly on this route. The exception EXC-0203 meant to cover it is invalid: it was self-approved by the requester (sofia.santos) who lacks the risk_owner role, violating EXC-1's requirement that an exception be approved by a risk_owner other than the requester.
Session code and policy parameters are not modified. The 15-minute privileged idle timeout remains unchanged.
The new reopen_payee in store.py only updates status and closed_at columns; no NPI fields (account_number, routing_number, tax_id, date_of_birth) are read or written in plaintext.
No integrations or transports code is modified. Outbound endpoints remain unchanged.
The service layer logs only the action name and payee_id (not NPI values); the handler returns a summarized payee. No new log call exposes NPI.
The new reopen_payee service method calls self._audit(actor, 'reopen_payee', f'payee:{payee_id}'), recording actor, action, target, and time. The sample audit test passes in CI.
No changes to audit.py or audit retention parameters. The hash-chain and 7-year retention are unaffected.
No retention or purge code is modified. Reopening a payee sets closed_at=NULL and status='open', so the retention query (which selects only closed payees past the cutoff) correctly excludes it.
No integrations code or asset inventory is modified. The integrations list is unchanged.

The new SQL in store.py is a fixed string literal ('UPDATE payees SET status = ?open?, closed_at = NULL WHERE id = ?') with payee_id bound as a parameter. No user data is interpolated into the statement text.
No payment approval or creation logic is modified. Maker-checker controls in payments.py are untouched.
Mortgage-mortgage obligation; no mortgage code is touched. Not affected.
Mortgage-mortgage obligation; no mortgage underwriting code is touched. Not affected.
No payment or dual-control code is modified. The dual-control threshold and approval logic are unchanged.
No release or idempotency code is modified. The find_release/add_release logic in store.py is unchanged.
Ticket CHG-25340 is approved by grace.kim (change_manager) and its components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.service, payments.store) cover all four files modified in the change.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa@fernbrook.example, who has the change_approver role for payments and is not the author (sofia.santos). Independent approval is satisfied.
Both approvals name commit 42d355f9…, which is the sole commit and the head. No later commits exist, so the approval covers exactly what is merged.

The CI run on the final commit 42d355f9… reports result 'failure' with 1 failing test: test_privileged_routes_require_mfa. The full test suite is not passing on the final commit, violating the requirement that CI must be green on the final commit.

The change touches security-sensitive components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.store). A security_review approval from ines.halvorsen (security_reviewer, platform-security team, not the author) is present for the same commit.

The change introduces a deviation from MFA-1 (privileged route without MFA). The only relevant exception, EXC-0203, was self-approved by the requester sofia.santos, who does not hold the risk_owner role. Per the policy, an exception must be approved by a person with the risk_owner role other than the requester; EXC-0203 is therefore invalid and cannot cover the deviation.

ACR-0404 (MFA-1 evidence at commit e5bf6465…) covers apps/baseline-payments/payments/routes.py, which this change modifies with a new route. This is a behavioural change (not comment/whitespace), so the evidence lapses. The replacement CI test fails, providing no new passing evidence for MFA-1.

summary: The change adds a POST /payees/{id}/reopen route whose action (manage_payees) is privileged per the approved access policy, yet it is declared with mfa=False, directly violating MFA-1. The exception EXC-0203 that was intended to cover this deviation is invalid: it was self-approved by the change's author, who lacks the risk_owner role required by EXC-1. The CI run on the final commit fails on the MFA control test, so CHG-4 is also violated. Additionally, the prior MFA-1 acceptance evidence (ACR-0404) lapses under LAP-1 because routes.py is behaviourally changed and no new passing evidence exists. These violations are critical-severity and warrant rejection.
